noscript: Enable JavaScript to analyse GPX files locally in your browser.
dropHint: Or drop one GPX file here. Your file is read locally, not uploaded.
multipleTracks: This file has multiple tracks. Choose a track:
terrainWarning: Warning: the rough area of the track (a coarse bounding box, not the track itself) and your IP address are sent to OpenStreetMap's Overpass service. Your GPX file is never uploaded.
statusChooseTrack: Choose a track before analysis begins.
statusAnalysed: Analysed {count, plural, one {# trackpoint} other {# trackpoints}} in {seconds, number, ::.0} s{worker, select, true { (background worker)} other {}}.
loadingWater: Loading water areas from OpenStreetMap (servers may take a while)…
noWater: No mapped water areas found. Speed/waypoint results remain available.
terrainUnavailable: Terrain data unavailable; local results retained ({reason}).
readingGpx: Reading GPX in a background worker…
confirmLarge: This file contains {count, number} trackpoints (more than 50,000). Processing may be slow and use battery. Continue?
manyWaypoints: Unusually many waypoints ({count, number}). Analysis will continue; check the results carefully.
fileTooLarge: File exceeds the maximum allowed size of 10 MB
dropOne: Drop exactly one GPX file at a time
sampleLoadFailed: Could not load the sample track ({status})
atLeastOneStrategy: At least one detection strategy must remain enabled. Previous results retained.
terrainDisabled: Terrain disabled. Speed was re-enabled so at least one local strategy remains active.
largeFile: Large file ({mb, number, ::.0} MB). Analysing it can take a while and uses your device's processor and battery, so a phone may get warm. {downloaded, select, true {Downloading it also uses mobile data.} other {The file is not uploaded, so this costs no data.}} Please keep this page open.
segmentHelp: Click a map line or table row to select a segment; click it again to deselect. Use Tab to reach segment buttons and Enter or Space to select. Escape clears the selection.
terrainIntro: Lakes and rivers from OpenStreetMap show where your track is really in the water, for more accurate swims. This is what makes TigerLegs terrain-informed.
terrainSent: What is sent: the rough area of the track (a coarse bounding box, not the track itself) and your IP address, to OpenStreetMap's Overpass service. Your GPX file is never uploaded.
